A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POFUL linear-bandit work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 8 and Figures 3–4 report original simulations on three synthetic scenarios and three real-world classification datasets.

after.justification: Section 7 retains those original simulations. Appendix C and Figure 5 additionally report an empirical eigenspace-alignment analysis.

M1.justification: The POFUL action-selection objective, pivot sampling, and TS-MR/Greedy-MR switching procedures remain unchanged. The revised geometric proofs do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both retain the random-action, contextual-bandit, and prior-mean-mismatch synthetic scenarios, plus Cardiotocography, JapaneseVowels, and Segment. Appendix C reuses synthetic Example 1 without introducing a distinct task or input environment.

E2.justification: Figures 3–4 retain LinTS, TS-Freq, OFUL, and Greedy as baselines against TS-MR and Greedy-MR. The new Figure 5 examines the same six algorithms.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces an additional diagnostic metric: the estimate's Rayleigh quotient normalized by the largest eigenvalue of V_t, tracked over time in Example 1. The original simulation dimensions, thresholds, horizons, and reward construction are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests the eigenspace-alignment mechanism discussed in Case 2 of Section 5.2 and Proposition 5. Figure 5 supplies empirical evidence for an observation previously discussed without a dedicated analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the original simulations over 100 runs and retain the same plotted uncertainty bands. Appendix C introduces no new seed disclosure, repeated-run count, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test.

E6.justification: The six original cumulative-regret plots in Figures 3–4 are identical across versions. Figure 5 adds alignment trajectories showing an initial decline followed by movement toward one for all six algorithms.

T1.justification: Lemma 2 extends its statement from H_t to E_t, supported by a new radial-intersection argument in Appendix A.2. Lemma 3 and Appendix A.3 revise eigenvalue conditions and selection rules, introducing an inconsistency in the claimed minimizing pair. The main regret theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both claim computable, instance-dependent regret bounds through confidence-ellipsoid geometry and course-corrected LinTS/Greedy algorithms with minimax-order guarantees while retaining desirable empirical behavior. The rewritten abstract and contribution bullets preserve this scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C interprets alignment across the examined algorithms as evidence of a tendency associated with online decision-making. It also attributes the initial alignment decline to regularized least squares when the number of observations is below the dimension.

D1.justification: Simulation-generation instructions, thresholds, and classification-to-bandit construction are retained. Algorithm 1 adds lambda to its input list, but that regularization parameter was already defined and used in v2. No new code-access or computing-resource information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds spectral-bandit references and distinguishes graph-based low-rank methods from action-covariance geometry. It also expands the comparison with Hamidi and Bayati's thinness coefficient and adds UCB/Thompson-sampling background citations. These are targeted extensions of the existing positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution bullets are revised, with keywords and an organization subsection added. The former Section 6 becomes Section 5.3, two remarks exchange order, and references move after the appendices. Most technical and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: The paper receives document-wide changes to typography, spacing, heading styles, page headers, and caption formatting. Figure 1 becomes a two-panel illustration with an added projection diagram, and Figure 5 is new. Existing figures are retained and reflowed within the new layout.

improvement.justification: The expanded Appendix A.2 argument and new Appendix C diagnostic strengthen the geometric explanation and its empirical support. However, Appendix A.3 replaces v2's minimum-above/maximum-below eigenvalue definitions with maximum-above/minimum-below choices, inconsistent with the claimed adjacent minimizing pair. These opposing changes to theoretical support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
